# Ticket 02

## Title

Autopopulate Unit Type and Unit Size

## Description

In the "CONDENSER TYPE" section:
- When a user selects the Condenser Type and the Refrigerant from their dropdowns, we should populate the Unit Type dropdown filtered by the condenser type and the refrigerant that was selected.
- After a user selects a Unit Type, we should populate the Unit Size dropdown filtered by the Refrigerant + Unit Type that was selected

## Acceptance Criteria

When we select the Condenser Type and the Refrigerant we should see the Unit Type dropdown filtered by Condenser Type + Refrigerant selected.
When we select the Unit Type, we should see the Unit Size dropdown filtered by Refrigerant + Unit Type selected.

## Relevant Discussion
The Refrigerants comes from an unitdesign api GET /dropdowns
the attribute to get Unit Type is SDCommonUnitTypeRefrigerant
for example, we sould filter by the "parent" that contains the refrigerant selected.
  "SDCommonUnitTypeRefrigerant": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "display": "CU",
      "value": "CU",
      "parent": [
        "R-410A",
        "R-454B"
      ],
      "isActive": true
    },
    {
      "id": 2,
      "display": "CUE",
      "value": "CUE",
      "parent": [
        "R-410A",
        "R-454B",
        "R-513A"
      ],
      "isActive": true
    },..
]

The attribute for Unit Size is SDCommonUnitModelSizes
for example, we sould filter by the "parent" that contains both the refrigerant and the Unit Type selected.
	
"SDCommonUnitModelSizes": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "display": "101",
      "value": "101",
      "parent": [
        "R-410A",
        "R-454B",
        "CU"
      ],
      "isActive": true
    },
    {
      "id": 1,
      "display": "103",
      "value": "103",
      "parent": [
        "R-410A",
        "R-454B",
        "CU"
      ],
      "isActive": true
    },...
]

interpreterResult.requirementSummary: Populate Unit Type from Condenser Type and Refrigerant, then populate Unit Size from Refrigerant and Unit Type.
businessRules: Selecting Condenser Type and Refrigerant filters Unit Type by both selections.
Selecting Unit Type filters Unit Size by Refrigerant and Unit Type.
Always exclude entries with isActive=false.
developerConsiderations: Retrieve dropdown data from unitdesign GET /dropdowns.
Use SDCommonUnitModelSizes parent entries containing the selected Refrigerant and Unit Type.
ambiguities: The Condenser Type mapping is unclear because the example parent data contains refrigerants.
Empty filter-result behavior is unspecified.
Case sensitivity and downstream selection reset behavior are unspecified.

# Ticket 01

## Title

Calculate the DX Coil Height

## Description

As we enter in the Cooling Package (e.g. R-454B FW 43 ) - the system will run to Calculations and get the starting values.
The DX Coil Height is empty.
What we want to happen is:
- The Cooling Circuits are populated
- Then we sum the height for each Circuit to make the value that is to appear in the DX Coil Information.
- For exmaple We have 3 circuits, each with a height of 7.5
- so 7.5 + 7.5 + 7.5 = 22.5
- and should the user alter the Circuit Height - the form should react to this edit - resum all heights and update the Height field in DX Coil Information

interpreterResult.requirementSummary: Populate Cooling Circuits for a Cooling Package, sum their heights into DX Coil Height, and update the total when a Circuit Height is edited.
businessRules: Entering a Cooling Package runs calculations and populates Cooling Circuits.
DX Coil Height is the sum of all populated Cooling Circuit heights.
developerConsiderations: Update DX Coil Information when a Circuit Height is edited.

# Ticket 03

## Title

FW Series: Condenser Configuration Inputs

## Description

Business value: Captures the detailed physical and environmental parameters for Air Cooled (AC) and Evaporative Cooled (EC) condensers, as well as per-circuit refrigeration configurations, enabling accurate ECS calculations.

When the user selects the Condenser Type "AC" or "EC", the corresponding input fields should be displayed.

### Condenser Inputs — Air Cooled (AC)

| Row | Detail | Input Type | Source | Unit | Default / Options | Notes |
|-----|--------|------------|--------|------|-------------------|-------|
| 1 | Design Ambient | Numeric Input | User / Default | °F / °C | 95°F | Echoed in output 3.7 |
| 2 | ASHRAE Summer Design | Numeric Input | User / Default | °F / °C | — | |
| 3 | Default Condenser | Checkbox | User | — | — | Condenser selection mode |
| 4 | High Amb. / Altit. Cond. | Checkbox | User | — | — | Condenser selection mode |
| 5 | Condenser Tube Material | Dropdown | User / Default | — | Copper | |
| 6 | Condenser Fin Material | Dropdown | User / Default | — | Aluminum | |
| 7 | Condenser Tube Size | Dropdown | User / Default | mm | 3/8, 3/8 w/ 1" spacing | |
| 8 | Condenser Fin Type | Dropdown | User / Default | — | Corrugated | |

### Condenser Inputs — Evaporative Cooled (EC)

| Row | Detail | Input Type | Source | Unit | Default / Options | Notes |
|-----|--------|------------|--------|------|-------------------|-------|
| 1 | Bank ID# | ID | System | — | — | |
| 2 | Copies of this Bank | Numeric Input | User | — | — | |
| 3 | EC Model | Dropdown | User | — | — | See Catalog |
| 4 | Wet Bulb Temperature | Numeric Input | User | °F / °C | — | |


## Acceptance Criteria

Given the AC/EC condenser parameters and per-circuit cooling configurations, 
When processed, 
Then the system outputs condenser and circuit-level configuration ready for ECS calculation.

Given the user is configuring an AC condenser, 
When they enter ambient design conditions and coil geometry, 
Then the system records the condenser parameters.

Given the user is configuring an EC condenser, 
When they enter the EC model and wet bulb temperature, 
Then the system records the EC condenser parameters.

Given the user configures an AC condenser, 
When they select Condenser Passes, 
Then the system shall display AutoOdd, AutoEven, and 2 through 41 in increments of 1 as options.

Given the user configures an AC condenser, 
When they select Roof Type, 
Then the system shall display the specified dark and light roof type options with and without parapet/shrouding.

interpreterResult.requirementSummary: Configure AC and EC condensers.
businessRules: AC means Evaporative Cooled and EC means Air Cooled.

# Ticket 04

## Title

FW Series: UI Input validation and ranges for Coil Height

## Description
Coil Height of Water/Steam coils must be a multiple of specified value, round input to closest: 3/8" & 1/2" tube → multiple of 1.25"; 5/8" tube → multiple of 1.50"; 1" tube → multiple of 2.25"; Lamiflo coil → multiple of 9"; 3/8" tube w/ 1" spacing → multiple of 1"

## Acceptance Criteria

- Valid range: 1.25" to 100"
- The entered value must be a multiple of a coil-specific increment.
- If the entered value is not an exact multiple, round it to the nearest valid increment.
- Height increments by coil type/configuration:
  - 3/8" tube or 1/2" tube: Increment = 1.25"
  - 5/8" tube: Increment = 1.50"
  - 1" tube: Increment = 2.25"
  - Lamiflo coil: Increment = 9.00"
  - 3/8" tube with 1" spacing: Increment = 1.00"
- Examples:
  - Tube Size = 3/8" User enters 14.1" Nearest valid value = 13.75" (11 × 1.25)
  - Tube Size = 5/8" User enters 14.0" Nearest valid value = 13.5" (9 × 1.5)
  - Tube Size = 1" User enters 16.0" Nearest valid value = 15.75" (7 × 2.25)
  - Lamiflo coil User enters 20" Nearest valid value = 18"

interpreterResult.requirementSummary: Validate Water/Steam Coil Height within 1.25 to 100 inches and round to the nearest valid coil-specific increment.
businessRules: Coil Height must be a multiple of its coil-specific increment.
Non-multiple inputs are rounded to the nearest valid increment.
The 3/8-inch or 1/2-inch tube increment is 1.25 inches.
The 5/8-inch tube increment is 1.50 inches.
The 1-inch tube increment is 2.25 inches.
The Lamiflo coil increment is 9.00 inches.
The 3/8-inch tube with 1-inch spacing increment is 1.00 inch instead of the generic increment.
developerConsiderations: Use the specified coil/configuration increments and preserve the special spacing override.

# Ticket 04

## Title

FW Series: UI Input validation and ranges for Coil Height

## Description
Coil Height of Water/Steam coils must be a multiple of specified value, round input to closest: 3/8" & 1/2" tube → multiple of 1.25"; 5/8" tube → multiple of 1.50"; 1" tube → multiple of 2.25"; Lamiflo coil → multiple of 9"; 3/8" tube w/ 1" spacing → multiple of 1"

## Acceptance Criteria

- Valid range: 1.25" to 100"
- The entered value must be a multiple of a coil-specific increment.
- If the entered value is not an exact multiple, round it to the nearest valid increment.
- Height increments by coil type/configuration:
  - 3/8" tube or 1/2" tube: Increment = 1.25"
  - 5/8" tube: Increment = 1.50"
  - 1" tube: Increment = 2.25"
  - Lamiflo coil: Increment = 9.00"
  - 3/8" tube with 1" spacing: Increment = 1.00"
- Examples:
  - Tube Size = 3/8" User enters 14.1" Nearest valid value = 13.75" (11 × 1.25)
  - Tube Size = 5/8" User enters 14.0" Nearest valid value = 13.5" (9 × 1.5)
  - Tube Size = 1" User enters 16.0" Nearest valid value = 15.75" (7 × 2.25)
  - Lamiflo coil User enters 20" Nearest valid value = 18"

# Ticket 02

## Title

Autopopulate Unit Type and Unit Size

## Description

In the "CONDENSER TYPE" section:
- When a user selects the Condenser Type and the Refrigerant from their dropdowns, we should populate the Unit Type dropdown filtered by the condenser type and the refrigerant that was selected.
- After a user selects a Unit Type, we should populate the Unit Size dropdown filtered by the Refrigerant + Unit Type that was selected

## Acceptance Criteria

When we select the Condenser Type and the Refrigerant we should see the Unit Type dropdown filtered by Condenser Type + Refrigerant selected.
When we select the Unit Type, we should see the Unit Size dropdown filtered by Refrigerant + Unit Type selected.

## Relevant Discussion
The Refrigerants comes from an unitdesign api GET /dropdowns
the attribute to get Unit Type is SDCommonUnitTypeRefrigerant
for example, we sould filter by the "parent" that contains the refrigerant selected.
  "SDCommonUnitTypeRefrigerant": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "display": "CU",
      "value": "CU",
      "parent": [
        "R-410A",
        "R-454B"
      ],
      "isActive": true
    },
    {
      "id": 2,
      "display": "CUE",
      "value": "CUE",
      "parent": [
        "R-410A",
        "R-454B",
        "R-513A"
      ],
      "isActive": true
    },..
]

The attribute for Unit Size is SDCommonUnitModelSizes
for example, we sould filter by the "parent" that contains both the refrigerant and the Unit Type selected.
	
"SDCommonUnitModelSizes": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "display": "101",
      "value": "101",
      "parent": [
        "R-410A",
        "R-454B",
        "CU"
      ],
      "isActive": true
    },
    {
      "id": 1,
      "display": "103",
      "value": "103",
      "parent": [
        "R-410A",
        "R-454B",
        "CU"
      ],
      "isActive": true
    },...
]
